report:
Fresh full review of unique_names after the latest shared-file association-only delta. The new implementation_references marker in spec.rs does not change naming behavior; the complete current claim, sole ordinary implementation file, six ordinary tests and sole TODO were independently reassessed.

Requirements include well-formed full names, one canonical definition in the Design inventory, errors for malformed markers/duplicates, chapter-derived identities and renaming on namespace moves, ASCII dotted identifiers, paragraph-contiguous opening prose, identical syntax inside Sage prose, and full-name references that do not define another rule. Independently testable behavior is an authoring/review obligation, not something identifier syntax can prove.

The associated duplicate-insertion loop in add_chapter_text checks the shared anchors map after qualification and diagnoses duplicate full names while retaining the first definition. The captured file also contains valid_anchor_name (ASCII identifier components), paragraph/role/single-backtick/nonempty-prose checks, chapter_namespace (Design prefix, README treatment, hyphen normalization, invalid component rejection), and qualified namespace plus local-name composition. Both Markdown and dedented Sage prose reach the same parser/insertion path. References are parsed into a separate collection and resolved against definitions after inventory loading, never inserted as definitions. Moving to a different chapter namespace consequently computes a different full name and leaves unupdated old references dangling; this is not automatic migration. The linked anchor_moves claim was captured to confirm that compatibility-link/migration policy is separate context, not a claim that the current name parser rewrites consumers.

All six ordinary test bodies were read. canonical_inventory_uses_configured_chapters_and_local_names asserts exactly the expected README-derived and normalized hyphenated names, correct namespace/context, and exclusion of tenets/RFD definitions. chapter_namespace_collisions_and_duplicate_local_rules_are_errors requires both namespace-collision and duplicate-full-name diagnostics and rejects dotted/outside-Design chapter paths. duplicate_names_are_rejected_across_documents requires one retained definition, one duplicate diagnostic attributed to the second document naming the first, and retention of the original file; validation preserves that error. malformed_roles_and_empty_or_misplaced_rules_are_errors enumerates fourteen malformed name/role/paragraph cases, including blank-separated prose, and requires diagnostics and no indexed anchor. reference_roles_validate_targets_but_ignore_code_examples requires exactly one actual reference, unknown-target and malformed-role diagnostics, and no false references from code examples. sage_prose_rules_have_precise_spans_model_owners_and_cross_source_references verifies valid chapter-qualified Sage names, exact rule content/source slices, model owners and context, and two cross-format references with exact original marker spans and no diagnostics. Its review-fragment assertion preserves exact claim content. The helpers source and BookFixture were captured and invoke real production parsing/loading; review claim construction was captured for that supplementary assertion.

The sole TODO definitions_across_markdown_and_sage preserves the broader cross-origin duplicate/reference/context/chapter-naming matrix, including fuller rename/move scenarios beyond the current examples. It is not treated as a passing behavioral test. Its explicit envelope-clause owner prerequisite remains unchanged and is relevant to the shared canonical_sources association: clause prose syntax, clause spans and stable owner representation must exist before that owner matrix can be asserted. Current ordinary coverage is substantial but does not silently complete this deferred matrix. The independently-testable-behavior requirement remains subject to substantive review of authored claims; this syntax checker does not claim semantic proof.

All aspects are accounted for by current code and assertions or the retained explicit TODO. No source edits or suite runs occurred in this review. Fresh start/read/record commands captured dependencies and current inputs; no prior verdict was blindly transplanted. No requested edits.
